content: 1. This information applies exclusively to the oral forms of both agents. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. Administer the medications at least one hour apart. 2. Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium carbonate can reduce the levels or effectiveness of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only to the oral forms of both agents. Adjust therapy as needed and monitor closely. 3. Products containing multivalent cations may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, potentially reducing their efficacy. Administer tetracyclines separately from these products and monitor the patient closely. 4. Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium carbonate can decrease the levels or effectiveness of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Adjust therapy as necessary and monitor closely. 5. Velpatasvir’s solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at a pH greater than 5. Administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir at least four hours apart from antacids. 6. Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium carbonate can significantly reduce the levels or effectiveness of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with an acid-reducing agent is unavoidable, administer sotorasib four hours before or ten hours after the antacid. 7. Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium carbonate can reduce the levels or effectiveness of vismodegib by altering its solubility and bioavailability due to changes in gastric pH. The impact on efficacy is unknown. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 8. Antacids are not intended for the treatment of peptic ulcers. If sodium or magnesium intake is restricted, consult a healthcare provider before using this medication. 9. Do not take the maximum dose of antacids for more than 14 days. 10. In patients with kidney disease, consult a healthcare provider before using antacids, as decreased renal function may lead to toxicity from aluminum or magnesium. 11. If heartburn persists after taking the medication, discontinue use and consult a healthcare provider. 12. Do not use antacids if you have difficulty swallowing. 13. Antacids may interact with certain prescription drugs. Consult a healthcare provider before taking this medication, as antacids can increase or decrease the absorption of concurrently administered oral drugs by altering gastrointestinal transit time, pH, or through cationic binding. 14. Pregnancy Category C: The effects of this medication on pregnancy are uncertain. 15. Lactation: It is unknown whether this medication is excreted in breast milk. 16. Pregnancy Category A: Generally considered safe. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
